The test image shows tomato leaves with a distinct whitish/powdery coating on the upper leaf surfaces, with some browning at leaf margins. The leaves appear to have a pale, dusty appearance across most of the plant. This strongly suggests **Powdery Mildew**.

Now I'll view one reference image to confirm.

The reference image shows early-stage powdery mildew with discrete white spots. The test image appears to be a more advanced stage where the white powdery growth has expanded to cover most of the leaf surfaces — consistent with the symptom description "eventually forming a dense white layer of growth that can cover entire leaves" with "leaves withering and dying while remaining attached."

Key evidence from test image:
- White/pale powdery coating covering upper leaf surfaces extensively
- Leaves pale and dull, not dark-spotted (rules out bacterial diseases)
- No concentric rings (rules out Early Blight)
- No olive mold on undersides visible (less likely Leaf Mold)
- Browning at margins consistent with late-stage powdery mildew necrosis
- Leaves still attached to stem while dying
